notes: Identity verified independently from the supplied text: title More is easier? Testing the role of fluency in the more-credible effect; author William J. Skylark; Judgment and Decision Making 16(3), May 2021, pp. 638–686; DOI header 10.1017/s1930297500007774; SOURCE_URL is the SJDM article PDF. The text includes methods, results, tables, references and appendix, and is a primary research report, not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF was supplied. Only n_r is assigned; other side/fields are placeholders. Study 2 and p. 12 locate the main comparative effect in Table 4 (printed p. 649), independently of row ordering or numeric matching. The paper explicitly prints final analysed Study 2 N=434 (219 Standard-mapping, 215 Reversed-mapping), but the main ANOVA has F(1,431). The source does not explicitly reconcile that denominator with the final participant count or document an exact model-specific N. Therefore 434 remains a candidate and n_r.value is null. No N was inferred from degrees of freedom, and no group sum was adopted. The first-trial ANOVA in footnote 2 and the dichotomised-response analysis in footnote 5 are different analyses and were not substituted. The main comparative test is located; uncertainty is confined to its exact analytic sample.
